official_sources: Planning appeals procedural guide post 1 April 2026
Leeds advertisement consent and deemed consent guidance

official_measurement_examples.name: Separate consent regime
official_measurement_examples.fact: Advertisement control is a separate consent process within planning and does not itself grant planning permission for development.

official_measurement_examples.name: Express versus deemed consent
official_measurement_examples.fact: Some classes benefit from deemed consent only when all class conditions and limitations are met; otherwise express consent is required.

official_measurement_examples.name: Amenity and public safety
official_measurement_examples.fact: Advertisement control is exercised in the interests of amenity and public safety, taking relevant plan provisions and other material factors into account.

official_measurement_examples.name: Eight-week determination
official_measurement_examples.fact: The national guidance states an application for express consent should be determined within 8 weeks unless a longer period is agreed in writing.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 appeal timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current appeals guidance states advertisement consent appeals must normally be submitted within 8 weeks and distinguishes applications before and after 1 April 2026 for procedural guidance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Listed building separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Advertisement consent does not replace listed building consent where works to a listed building require that separate consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Standard conditions
official_measurement_examples.fact: Advertisements benefiting from consent remain subject to applicable standard and class conditions; deemed consent is not unconditional permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Advertisement consent status does not establish land ownership, access rights, development capacity or final parcel yield.

core_rules: advertisement consent is separate from planning permission
deemed consent requires all class conditions
express consent is not ownership evidence
amenity and public safety remain the statutory focus
advertisement consent does not authorise highway occupation
advertisement consent does not prove structural safety beyond applicable conditions
local special-control areas can alter advertisement controls
historic appeal procedure must not be applied to post-April-2026 cases
no parcel advertisement clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
consent status does not calculate parcel yield
absence of express consent need does not mean no other consent is needed
planning policy does not replace the Advertisement Regulations
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, Planning Inspectorate, legislation.gov.uk and current local-authority sources checked 2026-07-26. Current 2026 appeal procedure was retained separately from the older advertisement control regime; no parcel promotion.
